key_insight: A training-free approach (BAMI) that uses a new Masked Prediction Distribution (MPD) attribution method can reveal and mitigate two systematic biases—precision bias from high-resolution screens and ambiguity bias from complex UI elements—improving GUI grounding without retraining models.
problem_solved: Existing GUI grounding models struggle in complex, high-resolution interfaces (e.g., ScreenSpot-Pro) due to systematic localization and ambiguity errors; the paper diagnoses these failure modes and provides a training-free mitigation strategy.
method: Introduce Masked Prediction Distribution (MPD) as an attribution tool to localize where and why grounding predictions fail.
Diagnose two primary biases: precision bias (errors caused by high image resolution) and ambiguity bias (errors caused by visually complex or similar interface elements).
Apply BAMI — a set of training-free mitigation techniques (e.g., resolution-aware post-processing and ambiguity-aware scoring/filtering) to correct biased predictions at inference time.
impact: Enables more reliable GUI agents by diagnosing and fixing systematic grounding errors without expensive model retraining, making deployment and iteration faster for practitioners.
visual_elements: Schematic of MPD: input UI image → masked regions → prediction distribution heatmaps highlighting responsible regions
Before/After comparison: original grounding outputs vs. BAMI-corrected outputs on high-resolution and complex UI examples
Bias breakdown chart: bar or pie chart showing proportion of errors due to precision bias vs. ambiguity bias
Flow diagram of BAMI pipeline: MPD attribution → bias diagnosis → training-free mitigation → corrected prediction
paper_title: BAMI: Training-Free Bias Mitigation in GUI Grounding
paper_authors: Borui Zhang, Bo Zhang, Bo Wang, Wenzhao Zheng, Yuhao Cheng
